_: ElevenLabs text-to-sound prompts (eleven_text_to_sound_v2, 4 takes each = 200 credits). Generate the missing ones once, save as <name>/el_N.wav (48 kHz stereo). sfx.py prefers these over synthesis and varies pitch/EQ per use.
whoosh: Fast cinematic whoosh transition for a YouTube video edit, airy and clean with a short tail, 1.2 seconds
impact: Deep cinematic trailer impact hit, sub boom with a punchy transient and long reverb tail, 2.5 seconds
riser: Cinematic tension riser building up over 3 seconds, swelling strings and noise, ending abruptly
shimmer: Magical sparkle shimmer, glittering chimes rising and fading, dreamy, 2.5 seconds
pop: Soft bubbly UI pop for a number appearing on screen, clean and satisfying, 0.4 seconds
blip: Short digital UI blip, friendly notification tick, 0.3 seconds
heartbeat: Two slow deep human heartbeats, cinematic and close, low thump, 2 seconds
swish: Very short fast swish of air, quick cut transition, 0.4 seconds
stinger: Dramatic orchestral stinger, short brass and strings hit with reverb, 2 seconds
ding: Bright clean bell ding, correct answer, 1.5 seconds
phonebuzz: Smartphone vibrating twice on a wooden table, 1.5 seconds
phonering: Modern smartphone ringtone marimba melody, 3 seconds
cheer: Crowd of teenagers cheering and clapping in a school gym, 4 seconds
applause: Warm audience applause in a hall, 4 seconds
murmur: School canteen ambience, many people chatting, cutlery, 8 seconds, loopable
city: Night city street ambience, distant traffic and horns, 8 seconds, loopable
rain: Steady rain on a street with soft rumble, 8 seconds, loopable
wind: Soft wind on a rooftop at night, 8 seconds, loopable
roomtone: Quiet bedroom room tone, faint hum, 8 seconds, loopable
footstep: Single sneaker footstep on a school corridor floor, 0.4 seconds
freeze: Time freeze effect, sudden suck-in then airy shimmer, 2 seconds
carpass: Car passing by on a wet road at night, 3 seconds
